profile.headline: Graduate Student, MS CS @ Georgia Tech | Software Engineer @ MGM Resorts International
profile.summary:
I am a graduate student in Georgia Tech’s M.S. in Computer Science program, with a focus on Machine Learning. I hold a B.A. in Data Science from UC Berkeley, where I developed a strong foundation in probability, algorithms, and machine learning.

Alongside my academic pursuits, I work as a Software Engineer at MGM Resorts International, where I apply my technical skills in backend development and large-scale systems. My long-term goal is to advance toward research and engineering roles at the intersection of machine learning theory and applied systems.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
● Designed and built a REST API of a micro-service that adds comments and alerts to a customer reservation using a tablet (known as a lobby tool) instead of using a front-desk desktop. The service was built with .NET, Azure Web App Service, and the Opera Web Service API.

● Helped design and build a backend REST API of an audit logging service that stores data about employee actions when an employee looks up customer information using .NET, Azure Functions and a Cosmos DB.

● Implemented GraphQL queries and mutations for services that I built or updated.

● Built the backend of a web app service, using .NET and Azure Functions, that automates release notes. The web app provides support for multiple repositories and multiple release note configurations. The web app has drastically cut down the time it takes to create a release note.

● Converted all team services from using scope-based authorization to role-based authorization.

● Converted all team services from using Apigee Edge to using Apigee X proxies.

● Experience creating CI/CD pipelines using Azure DevOps (classic and YAML).

● Experience deploying all team services through Azure DevOps.

● Experience being a Site Reliability Engineer (on-call) for services of the Guest Services team.

projects.title: Great Apes Classifier
projects.description: Using the fastai deep learning library, I fine-tuned a ResNet-18 CNN model to classify photos of Great Apes (Humans, Chimpanzees, Gorillas, and Orangutans). I exported the model to be used on a Gradio application hosted on HuggingFace Spaces. This project was inspired by following the fast.ai course.

projects.title: Spotify Genre Classifier
projects.description:
Comparing machine learning models in classifying the genres of different records in a Spotify dataset.

Exploratory data analysis and data cleaning is done on the dataset to allow for better classification.

The machine learning models that are trained and compared are Scikit-learn's SGDClassifier, K-Nearest Neighbors, and a Nueral Network.
